title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' axiomatics. In it, a space is replaced by a set M of 'pieces' (cells or figures) carrying several relations: X ≤ Y (X lies in the closure or boundary of Y, a face relation); X <° Y ('X lies in the interior of Y'); X |°| Y ('interiors disjoint'); and auxiliary relations <<, ||. L is the set of 'points', the minimal elements. The 'shadow' of X is omb(X) = {a ∈ L | a ≤ X} and its interior part is omb(X)° = {a ∈ L | a <° X}. Axiom Mag L1 requires omb(X)° ≠ ∅ for all X: every piece has an interior point. Mag L2 is a stronger point-richness axiom.

Definition (trivial magasin): <° is equality and |°| is inequality, so only ≤ remains free. Grothendieck observes, 'trivially', that every poset (M, ≤) with these choices satisfies the magasin axioms. In modern terms this is the face poset of a regular cell complex: open cells are pairwise disjoint, and no cell lies in the interior of another.

Example 1 lists the induced relations:
- X << Y ⇔ X ≤ Y;
- a second relation is always satisfied;
- X || Y ⇔ the lower sets X̃ = M_{≤X} and Ỹ are disjoint, i.e. {X, Y} has no common lower bound.

With L = the minimal elements, omb(X) is the set of minimal elements below X. Since <° is equality, omb(X)° = ∅ if X ∉ L and = {X} if X ∈ L. Hence Mag L1 holds iff every element is minimal, i.e. the order is discrete. So a trivial magasin never satisfies Mag L1, and a fortiori not Mag L2, unless it is 'discretely trivial' (X ≤ Y ⇔ X = Y).

The moral: purely combinatorial cell posets are not 'point-rich' in his sense, so the L-axioms separate set-like models from combinatorial ones.

The page then begins the notion of a figure indexed by a poset I: a figure F together with an order isomorphism I ≅ F̃, i ↦ X_i. The next page characterises such maps φ: I → M as increasing, injective maps that induce isomorphisms I_{≤i} ≅ M_{≤X_i} and send distinct indices to pairs with disjoint interiors.

The left margin lists equivalent conditions for a magasin to be trivial, e.g. (v) X ≠ Y ⇒ X |°| Y and (vi) X <° Y ⇒ X = Y. These are only partly legible.
errors: No mathematical error found. The computation of omb(X)° and the conclusion that Mag L1 forces a discrete order are correct, given omb(X)° = {a ∈ L | a <° X}.
Mag L2 'a fortiori' failing presupposes that Mag L2 implies Mag L1 (defined on earlier pages); this cannot be checked from this page alone.
The claim that every poset yields a magasin is asserted as 'trivially verified' without checking the axioms on the page.
Several marginal conditions (ii)-(iv) are illegible, so the list of equivalent characterisations of triviality cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Trivial magasin: a poset with interior-inclusion equal to equality and interior-disjointness equal to inequality; any poset gives one.
ideas.modern_name: face poset of a regular CW / cell complex, viewed as a 'stratified' combinatorial space (cf. Alexandrov topology of a poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: face posets of regular cell complexes: Björner (1984) and the combinatorial topology tradition; poset spaces: Alexandrov (1937)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished (Analysis situs notes, 1986). Esquisse d'un programme only announces 'topologie modérée' in general terms.

ideas.what: Shadow omb(X) and interior shadow omb(X)°, with axiom Mag L1 (every piece has an interior point); trivial magasins satisfy it only when the order is discrete.
ideas.modern_name: point-richness / 'enough points' condition separating set-theoretic models from purely combinatorial cell structures (cf. locales vs spaces, spatiality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct modern counterpart for this specific axiom

ideas.what: Figures indexed by a poset I (order isomorphism I ≅ F̃), characterised on the next page as increasing injective maps that induce isomorphisms on lower sets and send distinct indices to interior-disjoint pieces.
ideas.modern_name: embeddings of a face poset / combinatorial realisation of a cell complex inside a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in the combinatorics of cell complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly tests his point axioms (Mag L1, L2) against purely combinatorial (poset) models and shows they exclude all non-discrete ones. This documents a deliberate design choice: his 1986 analysis situs is not meant to be a theory of face posets, but requires 'enough interior points'. The point bears on any reconstruction of his tame-topology programme, but is a small, routine observation.
missed.quote: On voit donc qu'un magasin trivial ne satisfait jamais Mag L 1, et a fortiori jamais Mag L 2 — sauf s'il est discrètement trivial
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to historians and to anyone comparing Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' with o-minimal or stratified-space and combinatorial frameworks. It shows his axioms separate set-like from combinatorial models.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a routine sanity check: a degenerate example of his axiomatics, and a correct one-line computation that point axioms force a discrete order. It also starts a definition of poset-indexed figures. Interesting only as documentation of the unpublished 1986 'magasin' axiomatics, with no new result.
transcription_corrections: Header: the image reads 'Magasins triviaux'; the earlier page's 'magmas' and this page's 'magasins' seem to be used for the same structure.
'L = ens des éléments minimaux de X' — the image looks like 'minimaux de M' (or 'en X' miswritten); L should be the set of minimal elements of M, not of X.
The second line of '1. Ex.' (transcribed 'X ≪̸ Y toujours satisfait') is uncertain in the image. It is some relation symbol declared always satisfied, possibly not a negated <<.
'omb' (ombre) is correct on this page; the previous page's 'amb°' is probably the same notion, 'omb°'.
'{+trivialement+}' is an insertion above 'on vérifie', which fits the image.
The crossed-out phrase at the start of 'Mais on vérifie … que pour tout ensemble ordonné' contains 'tout'/'tous' struck out; meaning unchanged.
